title: Close mask polygon contours at image boundaries
body:
### Motivation and context

Closes #11479.

Calling `find_contours` directly on an image-sized mask leaves contours open at the image edge. A fully foreground mask has no contour, and border-touching regions can be dropped or converted into truncated polygons.

Add a one-pixel background border for contour extraction, then subtract its coordinate offset. Keep the existing orientation filtering, approximation tolerance, too-few-points fallback, and RLE path.

### How has this been tested?

- Exact final commit: `5a1d116137b4410ad0f48287b55a8e7b58c9ef09`.
- Native generated SDK, PyTorch tensors, and scikit-image.
- Final validation: https://github.com/Afloat16/cvat/actions/runs/43306800851
- 24 new tests pass; the original implementation has 19 failures and 5 passing controls.
- 48 existing mask/attribute unit controls pass.
- Black and isort checks pass.

The regressions compare each edge/corner and full-image foreground mask with the same region translated into a larger image with background. They cover probabilities of exactly 0.5 and 1.0, disconnected border components, and unchanged interior-hole filtering, approximation, empty masks, and RLE output.

The coordinates keep the existing pixel-center interpolation convention, so an outer contour can extend approximately half a pixel beyond the image boundary. The conversion allocates one padded mask. This validation concerns geometry and annotation preservation, not model quality, GPU performance, or a running CVAT server.

### Checklist

- [x] Based on `develop`.
- [x] Added a changelog fragment and regression tests.
- [x] Kept the ordinary interior contour and RLE behavior.
- [x] Documentation impact: no public API change.
